entities.name: PMID:25096285
observations: Retrospective 10-eye severe-glaucoma pilot combined glaucoma drainage implant surgery with injectable crosslinked/reticulated hyaluronic acid gel over 2 years.
Mean IOP decreased from 38.5±10.7 to 13.0±5.0 mmHg; reported success was 80% at ≥40% reduction and 50% at ≥50% reduction.
Small uncontrolled design supports feasibility but cannot establish efficacy or comparative benefit.

entities.name: PMID:22167544
observations: In 55 eyes undergoing deep sclerectomy, crosslinked sodium hyaluronate (HEALAflow) was associated with mean IOP reduction from 21.6 to 11.5 mmHg and medication reduction from 2.4 to 0.5.
Five eyes had hypotony below 6 mmHg and three had iris incarceration; this is indirect evidence because the procedure was nonpenetrating.

entities.name: PMID:33913846
observations: Prospective 60-eye trabeculectomy comparison found similar 12-month IOP reduction and complications with HealaFlow versus low-dose mitomycin-C, without clear HealaFlow superiority.

entities.name: PMID:26171243
observations: Retrospective 40-eye case-control trabeculectomy study found no meaningful HealaFlow advantage in final IOP or medication burden versus control.

entities.name: HealaFlow
observations: Crosslinked sodium hyaluronate/reticulated hyaluronic acid gel used as a glaucoma surgical adjunct in indirect human studies.
Exact product formulation, dose, placement, and use in the direct tube-implant pilot require confirmation before protocol development.

entities.name: Severe glaucoma
observations: Direct pilot population had severe glaucoma defined by visual-field loss worse than -20 dB and underwent drainage implant surgery.

entities.name: HA tube-shunt pilot rationale
observations: A prospective feasibility/safety pilot is justified, but evidence is insufficient for routine use or a definitive efficacy claim.

Key unresolved outcomes include medication burden, capsule fibrosis/encapsulation, hypotony, inflammation, infection, tube/plate complications, reoperation, corneal effects, and long-term gel persistence.
A contemporaneous tube-only comparator and at least 24 months of follow-up would improve interpretability.
